explanation: The refactored backend uses the scenario-selected Ontario charging shape and time mapping for shared LDV chargers. Compare the actual hourly values and normalization with the legacy BEV profile; the selected travel source is charging_profiles.travel_behavior_source. Legacy notes describe a 0.20 mean, but the supplied hourly table has a peak of 1 and a mean near 0.449, so those notes alone cannot establish the cause of a shape difference.

Both representations use vehicle-class scaling factors to convert capacity into potential activity. The reviewed manual factors now assume 16 hours per day (5,840 hours per year), rather than the legacy 6,500 hours per year, with rounding to one decimal. For heavy trucks this gives 2.9 rather than 3.25 billion tonne-km per thousand vehicles. These are potential-activity assumptions; observed utilization is represented separately by annual capacity factors, whose denominator also contains this scaling factor.

Charger fixed costs retain a 1% relationship to capital costs in both versions. Review differences in charger composition, cost input years, currency conversion and cohort representation; the refactored backend applies reviewed national port shares and the earliest available cost rates to existing chargers. The 1% relationship itself is not a changed assumption.

Marine costs replace legacy OEO vessel costs weighted by ICCT Great Lakes-St Lawrence activity with a CIMS capital-cost/service-output baseline and reviewed relative factors. This changes the cost level, not the billion-tonne-km unit scale. Road costs use selected ATB retail prices divided by the configured markup and current fleet weights instead of legacy Autonomie manufacturing prices and earlier weights; missing gasoline/CNG options use diesel proxies. Aircraft use CIMS capital cost divided by FAA annual service output instead of legacy freight cost ratios. Source currency years and provisional metadata remain separate review cues.

Marine maintenance applies the reviewed OEO class ratio to the CIMS service-capital baseline; legacy costs aggregate vessel-type OEO/ICCT evidence. The legacy marine numeric OPEX/CAPEX ratio does not reproduce its note's simple 5% relationship, leaving its additional normalization unresolved. This cost-baseline change drives large marine differences without a billion-tonne-km unit conversion. Other drivers are LDV repair/MSRP and age assumptions, BEAN truck proxies and payloads, purchase-price-scaled bus maintenance, and FAA service-normalized aircraft costs. Legacy gasoline trucks also cite an AFLEET ratio; intercity buses cite a separate class ratio.

Legacy marine and other off-road notes divide 2021 provincial energy by mean 2015-2019 national intensity; the refactored backend uses energy and intensity from the same configured observation year. This service-baseline change is a direct review target for the large marine-demand difference, alongside updated CEUD evidence and CER GDP projections. Legacy demand notes cite the COVID-affected 2021 baseline and CER Energy Futures 2023. Read demand.future_car_demand from the current scenario for GDP-indexed growth versus the optional extrapolated car/light-truck split.

Legacy urban gasoline-bus notes apply a GREET gasoline factor to CEUD diesel intensity; current historical values backcast an ATB diesel-proxy bus level with the CEUD class intensity trend and occupancy. Replacing that gasoline-specific penalty is a direct driver of the bus difference. LDVs use Canadian ratings and relative ATB improvements with MTO weights, replacing legacy absolute Autonomie projections and Wards weights. Other drivers include truck/vocation weights, missing-powertrain proxies, PHEV energy weighting and off-road CEUD/REGEN/GREET factors. These mechanisms identify review targets without quantitatively decomposing each delta.

Freight-light-truck HEV differences chiefly concern fuel composition: legacy notes select pickups/vans with commercial MTO ages; current rules include multi-purpose vehicles, mapped Report A ages and the registered annual fuel-share series. The fuel-share audit reconstructs each cohort; the very small legacy HEV denominator magnifies percentage changes. Road totals also move from the legacy 2021 stock anchor to the configured observation year with survival redistribution. Off-road turnover reconciles annual activity; chargers derive from BEV stock/public ports instead of energy consumption. The additional 2023 capacity is unmatched coverage, never zero legacy stock.

The refactored backend can supply NHTSA light/medium-vehicle and NEMS heavy-truck survival schedules, aggregated to model age blocks using current class weights. The supplied legacy database has no survival-curve table, so this is one-sided representation coverage with no numerical legacy ranking. Review the source schedules and fixed-lifetime relationship without treating absent legacy curves as zero survival.

Compare only technologies represented by fixed lifetimes in both databases. Aircraft now use the reviewed CIMS lifetime of 30 years; legacy aircraft use a 24-year median from Boeing's economic-life study. Legacy road rows include NHTSA median and MOVES heavy-truck values; the refactored backend can instead represent selected classes with NHTSA/NEMS survival curves. Bus lifetimes follow supported provincial and powertrain-specific StatCan evidence, while other technologies use reviewed category lifetimes. Fixed-versus-curve coverage is a representation difference and must not be interpreted as a missing lifetime of zero.

Legacy road notes use 2021 utilization for the first period and the 2015-2019 average thereafter, with a minimum at 99.9% of the maximum. Current utilization uses the latest five eligible years excluding 2020-2021, and the changed capacity-to-activity scaling changes the activity / (stock times scaling) denominator. Legacy bounds index operating periods while current bounds index vintages, so retain that applicability distinction during comparison. Charger bounds follow reviewed cohort-year assumptions; the prepared age-dependent road trajectories remain outside the current database seam.

Legacy PHEV blend notes describe averages across vehicle classes and model years. Current blends sum class-weighted electrical and total energy before taking their ratio, then average future endpoints; existing LDV representatives use category-specific range weights. These are fuel-input proportions, distinct from the excluded vehicle market-share constraints. Compare only supported equivalent blend technologies.
